title: Growth Sprint Playbook: Dedicated -> Private Migration & SLA Expansion
content:
Purpose:
This is a practical, sprint-oriented playbook for Customer Success to convert mid-to-large accounts on Dedicated capacity into Private deployments (VPC/on-prem) and/or to sell premium SLA add-ons. Treat as a modular kit: use the QBR templates, renewal tracker format, technical readiness checklist, and outreach sequences in any combination.

High-level objective:
- Close Dedicated -> Private migration or SLA expansion within a 3–6 month growth sprint for target accounts that meet the signals below.
- Improve ARR per account by selling Private deployment or Premium SLA + Dedicated upsell.

Signals that indicate good fit for this play:
- Regular sustained dedicated spend >= $30k/month or predictable commit usage.
- Data residency / compliance concerns surfaced in support tickets, security reviews, or renewal conversations.
- Repeated latency/throughput demands that Dedicated is approaching capacity or requires isolated pools.
- Executive mentions of a roadmap requiring on-prem or VPC for regulated features.
- Account has had recent production incidents where SLA guarantees would materially change risk tolerance.
- High product integration depth (deep API usage across multiple services).

Account scoring rubric (quick):
Score 0–3 for each, target >=9 to qualify for aggressive outreach.
- Spend velocity (0–3): 0: <5k/mo, 1: 5–15k, 2: 15–30k, 3: >30k
- Compliance urgency (0–3): 0: none, 1: exploratory, 2: required in 12–18m, 3: required now
- Technical complexity (0–3): 0: low, 1: 1–2 integrations, 2: >2 integrations, 3: deep infra integration
- Exec sponsorship (0–3): 0: none, 1: influencer engaged, 2: champion identified, 3: exec sponsor confirmed

QBR agenda template (45–60m) — editable per account:
1) Quick health score: usage, latency, error rate (5m)
2) Business outcomes: runway, features using Redwood (10m)
3) Migration/expansion thesis: why Dedicated -> Private or SLA matters (10m)
4) Technical checklist & gap review (10m)
5) Commercial proposal & timeline (5m)
6) Risks & mitigations / next steps with owners (5–10m)

Renewal & expansion tracker header (copy into sheet):
Account,ARR Monthly,Current Product,Dedicated Spend Avg (30d),Last QBR Date,Compliance Flag (Y/N),Score,Primary Champion,Technical Lead,Decision Timeline,Expansion Ask,Proposed Value,Proto Offer ID,Next Touch Date,Owner,Status,Notes
Example row:
Acme Inc,120000,dedicated,34000,2026-01-08,Y,10,Olivia Ramos,Marco Li,Q3-2026,Private migration + premium sla,+55k ARR,PO-783,2026-02-14,Priya Shah,engaged,Waiting on security questionnaire response

Outreach sequences (multichannel) — 6 touchpoints stretched across 4 weeks:
- Day 0: Personal email from CSA/AM summarizing QBR learnings + one-sentence ask (meeting to review migration benefits). Template tokens: {{account}}, {{champion_name}}, {{usage_metric}}.
- Day 3: Short LinkedIn note to champion referencing recent QBR bullet.
- Day 7: Technical note to engineering lead with self-serve checklist + ask for 30–45m deep-dive.
- Day 14: Commercial proposal delivery with clear ROI slide and deployment timeline options.
- Day 21: Exec-level one-pager to VP/CTO with risk/benefit summary.
- Day 28: Final reminder + ask to schedule decision call before renewal cut.

Technical readiness checklist (for Private migration):
- Data residency & classification inventory completed (owner: customer SRE/security).
- Network topology: VPN/VPC peering requirements mapped.
- KMS/HSM requirements & current provider identified.
- Audit/logging retention targets confirmed.
- Required model set & versions to be hosted identified.
- Peak throughput & latency SLOs measured (95/99th percentiles).
- Storage and snapshot/export requirements documented.
- On-prem hardware validation (if applicable) — GPU counts, NICs, drivers.
- IT change windows and maintenance windows documented.
- Contractual constraints (e.g., cross-border data transfer) flagged.

Commercial constructs & example offers (playbook snippets):
- Private baseline: One-time deployment fee + monthly platform license (example: $45k setup + $30k/mo).
- Dedicated to Private migration bundle: Migration fee credit if commit >= 12 months (example: waive 50% setup fee).
- Premium SLA add-on: 99.95% + dedicated escalation path + 1-hour P1 response (example: +15–30% of committed monthly).
- Trial migration: 90-day pilot in VPC with reduced commit for new private customers (pilot pricing: 30% of full run-rate).
Note: always run pricing through Sales Ops; these numbers are illustrative.

Objection handling cheatsheet (short):
- "We can't justify cost": show per-token unit economics change and model latency/throughput improvements; provide 12–24 month ROI with avoided downtime scenarios.
- "Security concerns": offer architecture diagram, KMS/HSM integration options, SOC/Security artifact pack, and engineer-to-engineer session.
- "Timeline is too long": propose phased migration (control plane first, then models), short pilot, or hybrid (VPC with limited on-prem).

Roles & responsibilities (one-liners):
- Customer Success Lead / Owner: shepherds timeline, QBRs, executive comms.
- Solutions Engineer: technical readiness lead, runs deep-dive calls, provides architecture draft.
- Sales Rep: commercial negotiation, contract terms, discounts approvals.
- Deployment PM (professional services): project plan, milestone tracking.
- Security/Compliance SME (Redwood): provides artifacts, answers questionnaire.

Sprint milestones (example 16-week sprint):
- Week 0–2: Discovery + scoring + exec alignment
- Week 3–4: Technical deep-dive + PoC/pilot definition
- Week 5–8: Pilot execution (VPC or on-prem pilot)
- Week 9–12: Pilot evaluation, contract negotiation
- Week 13–16: Finalize deployment plan + cutover scheduling

Sample KPI dashboard (what to track during the sprint):
- Decision rate (meetings -> signed LOI)
- Time to pilot start (days)
- Pilot success rate (binary + outcome metrics: latency, cost delta, feature parity)
- Expansion ARR closed
- Churn risk delta post-engagement

QBR slide checklist (for CS to prepare):
- 1 slide: Account health snapshot (usage, spend, incidents)
- 1 slide: Business outcomes & product map
- 1 slide: Technical gap analysis (top 3 risks)
- 1 slide: Recommended commercial options + 1–2 pricing scenarios
- 1 slide: Migration timeline + dependencies + owners
- 1 slide: Ask and next steps

Playbook quick templates (email snippets):
Personal invite (to champion):
Subject: Quick follow-up from our QBR — migration option for {{account}}
Hi {{champion_name}},
Thanks again for the QBR conversation — I left with two clear signals: you need predictable capacity and a stronger compliance posture. I think a Private deployment plus our Premium SLA could remove those blockers. Can we book 30 minutes next week to go through a short technical checklist and a simple ROI for your team?
Best,
{{owner}}

Technical ask (to SRE):
Subject: Request: network & keys details for private pilot
Hi {{tech_lead}},
Quick list we need to scope the pilot: CIDR ranges, KMS provider, expected qps at peak, and any maintenance windows. If you can drop answers in this doc by EOD Friday we can produce an initial deployment plan.

Next steps / governance:
- Owner to create tracking row in central Renewal & Expansion tracker (sheet) after initial qualification.
- Book migration deep-dive within 7 business days post-QBR.
- Solutions Eng to produce Arc diagram & pilot plan within 10 business days.
- Commercial to deliver proposal within 3 business days of pilot sign-off.

Appendix — quick checklist for the first deep-dive call:
- Confirm legal & procurement timeline (yes/no/unknown)
- Confirm security questionnaire status and target date
- Decision stakeholders and sign-off authority
- Minimum necessary model set to migrate for pilot
- Any feature gaps that would block production parity

Notes / Known gaps in this draft:
- Numbers in "Commercial constructs" are illustrative; route all final pricing via Sales Ops.
- Add account-specific artifacts (previous incident postmortems, current infra diagrams) to linked_artifacts before sending to the customer.

If you use this doc: copy to the account folder, replace template tokens, paste the tracker row to the shared Expansion sheet, and tag the SRE/SE in Slack #cs-growth to start the intake.

Document history:
- v0.1 2025-11-12: initial draft (Priya)
- v0.2 2025-12-05: added pilot pricing options (Ethan)
- v0.3 2026-02-20: tightened outreach cadence and QBR template (Sana)
